title: Avatar
lead:
An Avatar is a graphical representation of a user, team, or entity.

Avatar can display an image, icon, or initials, and supports various sizes and shapes.

examples.name: Name
examples.description: The name is used to determine the initials displayed by the Avatar. It is also read by screen readers.

examples.name: Image
examples.description:
An avatar can display an image.
It is recommended to also include a name in addition to the image: the initials from the name are displayed while the image is loading, and the name makes the Avatar accessible to screen readers.

examples.name: Icon
examples.description: An avatar can display an icon. The icon will only be shown when there is no image or initials available.

examples.name: Badge
examples.description: An avatar can have a badge to indicate presence status. See the PresenceBadge component for more info.

examples.name: Badge Icon
examples.description: An Avatar can have a custom icon inside the badge.

examples.name: Shape: square
examples.description: An avatar can have a square shape.

examples.name: Color: brand
examples.description: An avatar can use the brand color from the theme's palette.

examples.name: Color: colorful
examples.description: An avatar can have the color be automatically picked based on the `name` prop (or `idForColor` can be used if a name is not available).

examples.name: Color: named color
examples.description: An avatar can have a specific named color from the theme's color palette  (e.g. `seafoam`, `grape`, or `pumpkin`)

examples.name: Active
examples.description: An avatar can communicate whether a user is currently active (for example, speaking or typing). Avatar supports `active`, `inactive`, and `unset`. The default is `unset`.

examples.name: Active Appearance
examples.description: An avatar can have different appearances when `active="active"`. Avatar supports `ring`, `shadow`, and `ring-shadow`. The default is `ring`.

examples.name: Initials: Custom Initials
examples.description:
An avatar can display custom initials by setting the initials prop. It is generally recommended to use
        the `name` prop instead, as that will automatically determine the initials and display them.

examples.name: Size
examples.description:
An avatar supports a range of sizes from 16 to 128. The default is 32. 

Avoid using sizes 16 and 20 for interactive Avatars, or ensure that there is at least 8px or 4px spacing respectively to meet WCAG target size requirements.

tables.name: Avatar
rows: The Avatar's image. Usage e.g.: `image={{ src: '...' }}`
`PersonRegular` (the default icon's size depends on the Avatar's size)
Icon to be displayed when the avatar doesn't have an image or initials.

(optional) Custom initials. It is usually not necessary to specify custom initials; by default they will be derived from the `name` prop, using the `getInitials` function. The initials are displayed when there is no image (including while the image is loading).

WithSlotShorthandValue<Omit<ComponentProps<Pick<BadgeSlots, "root" | "icon">>, "color"> & Pick<BadgeProps, "size"> & { status?: PresenceBadgeStatus; outOfOffice?: boolean; } & RefAttributes<HTMLDivElement>>
Badge to show the avatar's presence status.
Optional activity indicator * active: the avatar will be decorated according to activeAppearance * inactive: the avatar will be reduced in size and partially transparent * unset: normal display

The color when displaying either an icon or initials. * neutral (default): gray * brand: color from the brand palette * colorful: picks a color from a set of pre-defined colors, based on a hash of the name (or idForColor if provided) * [AvatarNamedColor]: a specific color from the theme

Specify a string to be used instead of the name, to determine which color to use when color="colorful". Use this when a name is not available, but there is another unique identifier that can be used instead.

The name of the person or entity represented by this Avatar. This should always be provided if it is available. The name is used to determine the initials displayed when there is no image. It is also provided to accessibility tools.
The avatar can have a circular or square shape.

Size of the avatar in pixels. Size is restricted to a limited set of supported values recommended for most uses (see `AvatarSizeValue`) and based on design guidelines for the Avatar control. Note: At size 16, if initials are displayed, only the first initial will be rendered. If a non-supported size is needed, set `size` to the next-smaller supported size, and set `width` and `height` to override the rendered size. For example, to set the avatar to 45px in size: `<Avatar size={40} style={{ width: '45px', height: '45px' }} />`
